titulo: Expressing Experiences and Connections Through Time and Place
titulo_es: Experiencias y conexiones a través del tiempo y el lugar
estandares: Narro experiencias personales conectadas con el presente. Relaciono ideas en el tiempo y por contraste, y ubico personas y hechos en el espacio.
competencias: Usar el presente perfecto para experiencias; confirmar información con tag questions; enlazar ideas con cláusulas de tiempo y contraste; describir personas, lugares de la casa y ocupaciones.
componentes: Pensamiento crítico, comunicación, colaboración y creatividad.

proyecto.descripcion_es: Cada estudiante entrevista a un familiar sobre sus experiencias de vida y escribe un perfil: qué ha hecho (present perfect), cuándo y dónde, y qué rasgos de personalidad y oficio lo definen.
proyecto.descripcion_en: Each student interviews a relative about their life experiences and writes a profile: what they have done (present perfect), when and where, and which personality traits and occupation define them.

lecciones.content_es:
Cómo se forma

have / has + participio pasado: I have visited Cartagena. · She has finished the project.

Para qué sirve

  • Experiencias sin decir cuándo: I've been to Peru.
  • Acciones pasadas con efecto en el presente: I've lost my keys (y sigo sin ellas).
  • Acciones que continúan: We've lived here for five years.

Palabras clave

ever, never, already, yet, just, so far, since, for.
Have you ever tried sushi? · I haven't finished yet. · She has just arrived.

La diferencia con el pasado simple

Si dices cuándo exactamente, va pasado simple: I visited Cartagena in 2023. Sin momento concreto: I have visited Cartagena.
lecciones.content_en:
How it is formed

have / has + past participle: I have visited Cartagena. · She has finished the project.

What it is for

  • Experiences with no stated time: I've been to Peru.
  • Past actions with a present effect: I've lost my keys (and I still don't have them).
  • Actions that continue: We've lived here for five years.

Key words

ever, never, already, yet, just, so far, since, for.
Have you ever tried sushi? · I haven't finished yet. · She has just arrived.

The difference from the simple past

If you say exactly when, use the simple past: I visited Cartagena in 2023. With no specific moment: I have visited Cartagena.

lecciones.content_es:
La coletilla de confirmación

Es la pregunta corta al final: You're from Cali, aren't you? Equivale a «¿verdad?».

La regla

Si la oración es afirmativa, la coletilla es negativa, y al revés:

  • She is a teacher, isn't she?
  • You don't smoke, do you?
  • They have finished, haven't they?

Cómo elegir el auxiliar

Se repite el auxiliar de la oración. Si no hay, se usa do/does/did: He plays guitar, doesn't he?

Casos especiales

  • I am late, aren't I?
  • Let's go, shall we?
  • Open the door, will you?
lecciones.content_en:
The confirmation tag

It is the short question at the end: You're from Cali, aren't you?

The rule

If the sentence is affirmative, the tag is negative, and the other way round:

  • She is a teacher, isn't she?
  • You don't smoke, do you?
  • They have finished, haven't they?

Choosing the auxiliary

You repeat the auxiliary of the sentence. If there is none, use do/does/did: He plays guitar, doesn't he?

Special cases

  • I am late, aren't I?
  • Let's go, shall we?
  • Open the door, will you?

lecciones.content_es:
Conectar dos momentos

Los conectores de tiempo unen dos acciones: when, while, before, after, as soon as, until, since, whenever.

  • When I got home, my mom was cooking.
  • While she was studying, the phone rang.
  • As soon as the bell rings, we leave.

La regla del futuro

Después de un conector de tiempo no se usa will, aunque el sentido sea futuro: I'll call you when I arrive, no when I will arrive.

La coma

Si la cláusula va primero, se separa con coma: After we finished, we went out. Si va al final, no lleva coma.
lecciones.content_en:
Connecting two moments

Time connectors join two actions: when, while, before, after, as soon as, until, since, whenever.

  • When I got home, my mom was cooking.
  • While she was studying, the phone rang.
  • As soon as the bell rings, we leave.

The future rule

After a time connector you do not use will, even if the meaning is future: I'll call you when I arrive, not when I will arrive.

The comma

If the clause comes first, separate it with a comma: After we finished, we went out. If it comes last, no comma.

lecciones.content_es:
Contraponer dos ideas

  • although / even though / though + oración: Although it was raining, we went out.
  • while / whereas para comparar dos sujetos: He likes rock, whereas she prefers pop.
  • but une dos oraciones: It was raining, but we went out.
  • however abre una oración nueva, con punto y coma o punto: It was raining. However, we went out.

Error frecuente

No se usan although y but en la misma oración: Although it was raining, but we went out es incorrecto. Se elige uno.

Con sustantivo

despite / in spite of van seguidos de sustantivo o gerundio: Despite the rain, we went out.
lecciones.content_en:
Contrasting two ideas

  • although / even though / though + clause: Although it was raining, we went out.
  • while / whereas to compare two subjects: He likes rock, whereas she prefers pop.
  • but joins two clauses: It was raining, but we went out.
  • however opens a new sentence: It was raining. However, we went out.

Common mistake

Do not use although and but in the same sentence: Although it was raining, but we went out is wrong. Choose one.

With a noun

despite / in spite of are followed by a noun or gerund: Despite the rain, we went out.

fichas.d: Aunque: introduce una idea que contrasta.
fichas.d_en: Introduces a contrasting clause.

fichas.d: A pesar de + sustantivo o gerundio, sin of después de despite.
fichas.d_en: Followed by a noun or gerund; no of after despite.

fichas.d: Mientras que: compara dos sujetos distintos.
fichas.d_en: Compares two different subjects.

fichas.d: Sin embargo: abre oración y va seguido de coma.
fichas.d_en: Opens a sentence and is followed by a comma.

quiz.why_en: A noun follows, so it takes despite.

lecciones.t: Preposiciones de lugar y de tiempo
lecciones.content_es:
Tiempo: in, on, at

  • in: meses, años, siglos, partes del día — in July, in 2026, in the morning
  • on: días y fechas — on Monday, on May 3rd, on my birthday
  • at: horas y momentos puntuales — at 7 o'clock, at night, at Christmas

Lugar: in, on, at

  • in: espacios cerrados y áreas — in the room, in Bogotá, in Colombia
  • on: superficies y líneas — on the table, on the wall, on the second floor
  • at: puntos exactos y direcciones — at the bus stop, at home, at 25 Fifth Street

Movimiento

to (hacia), into (hacia adentro), onto, from, through (a través), across (al otro lado), along (a lo largo).
lecciones.content_en:
Time: in, on, at

  • in: months, years, centuries, parts of the day — in July, in 2026, in the morning
  • on: days and dates — on Monday, on May 3rd, on my birthday
  • at: clock times and points — at 7 o'clock, at night, at Christmas

Place: in, on, at

  • in: enclosed spaces and areas — in the room, in Bogotá, in Colombia
  • on: surfaces and lines — on the table, on the wall, on the second floor
  • at: exact points and addresses — at the bus stop, at home, at 25 Fifth Street

Movement

to, into, onto, from, through, across, along.

lecciones.content_es:
La casa

hallway (pasillo), living room, dining room, kitchen, bedroom, bathroom, study (estudio), attic (ático), basement (sótano), balcony, backyard (patio trasero), roof (techo), fence (cerca).

La familia extendida

nephew (sobrino), niece (sobrina), grandchild, in-laws: mother-in-law, brother-in-law. stepfather / stepmother (padrastro y madrastra), half-brother, only child (hijo único), twins (gemelos), relatives (parientes).

Ojo

El plural de los compuestos con guion va en la primera palabra: mothers-in-law, no mother-in-laws.
lecciones.content_en:
The house

hallway, living room, dining room, kitchen, bedroom, bathroom, study, attic, basement, balcony, backyard, roof, fence.

The extended family

nephew, niece, grandchild, in-laws: mother-in-law, brother-in-law. stepfather / stepmother, half-brother, only child, twins, relatives.

Careful

The plural of hyphenated compounds goes on the first word: mothers-in-law, not mother-in-laws.

lecciones.content_es:
Rasgos positivos

kind (amable), generous, honest, reliable (confiable), hard-working, outgoing (extrovertido), patient, funny, confident (seguro de sí).

Rasgos negativos

selfish (egoísta), rude (grosero), lazy (perezoso), arrogant, stubborn (terco), moody (temperamental), unreliable.

Sinónimos

kind = nice, friendly, caring · smart = clever, bright, intelligent · shy = reserved, quiet, timid.

Antónimos con prefijo

un-: friendly → unfriendly, reliable → unreliable.
im-/in-/dis-: patient → impatient, polite → impolite, honest → dishonest, tolerant → intolerant.
lecciones.content_en:
Positive traits

kind, generous, honest, reliable, hard-working, outgoing, patient, funny, confident.

Negative traits

selfish, rude, lazy, arrogant, stubborn, moody, unreliable.

Synonyms

kind = nice, friendly, caring · smart = clever, bright, intelligent · shy = reserved, quiet, timid.

Antonyms with prefixes

un-: friendly → unfriendly, reliable → unreliable.
im-/in-/dis-: patient → impatient, polite → impolite, honest → dishonest, tolerant → intolerant.

lecciones.content_es:
Profesiones

teacher, doctor, nurse, engineer, lawyer (abogado), accountant (contador), architect, journalist, chef, mechanic, electrician, farmer (agricultor), firefighter, police officer, salesperson, designer, programmer.

Hablar del trabajo

  • What do you do? — I'm a nurse. (siempre con a/an)
  • She works as an engineer for a construction company.
  • He works in education / in a hospital.

Sufijos frecuentes

-er: teacher, farmer · -or: doctor, actor · -ist: dentist, journalist · -ian: musician, electrician.
lecciones.content_en:
Professions

teacher, doctor, nurse, engineer, lawyer, accountant, architect, journalist, chef, mechanic, electrician, farmer, firefighter, police officer, salesperson, designer, programmer.

Talking about work

  • What do you do? — I'm a nurse. (always with a/an)
  • She works as an engineer for a construction company.
  • He works in education / in a hospital.

Frequent suffixes

-er: teacher, farmer · -or: doctor, actor · -ist: dentist, journalist · -ian: musician, electrician.

repaso.resumen_es:
Lo esencial del periodo

El presente perfecto conecta el pasado con el ahora: sirve para experiencias, resultados presentes y acciones que continúan. Las cláusulas adverbiales ordenan las ideas en el tiempo y las contraponen, y las tag questions piden confirmación.

Puntos gramaticales

  • have/has + participio. for + duración, since + punto de inicio.
  • Si se dice cuándo exacto, va pasado simple.
  • Tag: afirmativa → negativa; se repite el auxiliar.
  • Sin will después de when, as soon as, until.
  • although + oración; despite + sustantivo. Nunca los dos con but.

Vocabulario

Preposiciones in/on/at de tiempo y lugar, partes de la casa, familia extendida, rasgos de personalidad con prefijos negativos y profesiones con a/an.
repaso.resumen_en:
The core of the term

The present perfect links the past with now: it serves for experiences, present results and actions that continue. Adverbial clauses order ideas in time and contrast them, and tag questions ask for confirmation.

Grammar points

  • have/has + participle. for + duration, since + starting point.
  • If the exact time is stated, use the simple past.
  • Tag: affirmative → negative; the auxiliary is repeated.
  • No will after when, as soon as, until.
  • although + clause; despite + noun. Never both with but.

Vocabulary

Prepositions in/on/at for time and place, parts of the house, extended family, personality traits with negative prefixes and professions with a/an.
